# 2 Samuel Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 169r–170v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_002_page_001.jpg, 2SA_002_page_002.jpg, 2SA_002_page_003.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** After this, David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?" The LORD said to him, "Go up." David said, "Where shall I go up?" And he said, "To Hebron."

**2** So David went up there, and his two wives also — Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite. **3** David brought up his men who were with him, every man with his household, and they settled in the cities of Hebron.

**4** And the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. When David was told, "The men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul," **5** he sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, "Blessed are you by the LORD, that you showed this covenant-faithfulness to your lord Saul and buried him.

**6** Now may the LORD show covenant-faithfulness and truth to you; and I also will repay you this kindness, because you have done this thing.

**7** Now let your hands be strong and be men of valor, for your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."

**8** But Abner the son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, had taken Ish-bosheth the son of Saul and brought him across to Mahanaim, **9** and he made him king over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel, over Ephraim, over Benjamin — over all Israel.

**10** Ish-bosheth the son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David. **11** The time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

**12** Abner the son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon. **13** Joab the son of Zeruiah and the servants of David marched out and met them at the pool of Gibeon. They sat down, one group on one side of the pool and the other on the other side.

**14** Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men arise and compete before us." Joab said, "Let them arise."

**15** So they arose and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David. **16** Each man seized his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent's side, and they fell together. So that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.

**17** And the battle was very fierce that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before the servants of David.

**18** The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was as swift of foot as a gazelle of the field. **19** Asahel pursued Abner, turning neither to the right nor to the left from following him.

**20** Abner looked behind him and said, "Is that you, Asahel?" He answered, "It is." **21** Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right or to your left — seize one of the young men and take his armor." But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.

**22** Abner said again to Asahel, "Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I then lift my face to your brother Joab?"

**23** But he refused to turn aside. So Abner struck him in the belly with the butt of his spear, and the spear came out through his back. He fell there and died on the spot. And all who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.

**24** But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. As the sun was setting, they came to the hill of Ammah, which is before Giah on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon. **25** The sons of Benjamin rallied behind Abner, formed one company, and took their stand on top of a hill.

**26** Abner called out to Joab: "Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? How long before you order your people to stop pursuing their brothers?"

**27** Joab said, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, the people would not have stopped pursuing their brothers until the morning."

**28** So Joab blew the trumpet, and all the people stopped. They pursued Israel no longer, and they fought no more.

**29** Abner and his men marched through the Arabah all that night, crossed the Jordan, passed through all of Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.

**30** Joab returned from pursuing Abner and assembled all the people. Nineteen of David's servants were missing, besides Asahel. **31** But David's servants had struck down three hundred and sixty of Benjamin and Abner's men.

**32** They took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father at Bethlehem. And Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at the break of dawn.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the narrative arc: David's anointing at Hebron (vv.1-7), Ish-bosheth's rival kingdom (vv.8-11), the encounter at Gibeon (vv.12-17), Asahel's death (vv.18-23), and the ceasefire (vv.24-32). The *hesed* theology in vv.5-6 is consistently recognized. The chapter establishes the central conflict of 2 Samuel 2-4: two kingdoms, two commanders (Joab and Abner), and the escalating blood-feud that will drive the narrative forward.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "inquired of" vs. "sought the LORD's direction"
- **EMET:** "inquired David of-YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "David inquired of the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "David sought the LORD's direction"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "David inquired of the LORD" — *sha'al ba-YHWH* is a technical term for oracular inquiry; "inquired of" is the standard rendering.

### V.2 — "wife of Nabal" vs. "widow of Nabal"
- **EMET:** "wife of-Naval"
- **LOGOS:** "wife of Nabal"
- **PNEUMA:** "widow of Nabal"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "widow of Nabal." PNEUMA correctly notes that Nabal is dead (1 Sam 25:38). The Hebrew *eshet* can mean wife or widow; "widow" is contextually accurate.

### V.5 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "covenant-faithfulness"
- **PNEUMA:** "faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "covenant-faithfulness" — project convention for *hesed* in covenantal contexts.

### V.7 — "sons of valor" vs. "valiant men" vs. "stand firm"
- **EMET:** "sons of-valor"
- **LOGOS:** "valiant men"
- **PNEUMA:** "Take courage and stand firm"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "men of valor" — balances EMET's literalism with natural English. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the specific Hebrew idiom *bney chayil*.

### V.9 — "Ashuri" vs. "Ashurites" vs. "Asher"
- **EMET:** "the-Ashuri"
- **LOGOS:** "the Ashurites"
- **PNEUMA:** "Asher"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the Ashurites." The Hebrew ha-Ashuri is debated — it may refer to the tribe of Asher or the Geshurites. "Ashurites" preserves the ambiguity of the MT.

### V.14 — "play" vs. "compete" vs. "have a contest"
- **EMET:** "let-them-play [yesachaqū]"
- **LOGOS:** "compete"
- **PNEUMA:** "have a contest"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "compete" — captures the organized, deadly character while preserving the euphemistic register of *sachaq*.

### V.16 — Place-name rendering
- **EMET:** "Chelqat ha-Tsurim [Field of-the-Flints/Sword-edges]"
- **LOGOS:** "Helkath-hazzurim"
- **PNEUMA:** "Field of Sword-Edges"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Helkath-hazzurim" — conventional English transliteration per standard Bible practice.

### V.17 — "exceedingly hard" vs. "very fierce" vs. "savage"
- **EMET:** "exceedingly hard"
- **LOGOS:** "very fierce"
- **PNEUMA:** "savage"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "very fierce" — accurate and measured. PNEUMA's "savage" adds connotation not in *qashah me'od*.

### V.22 — "How could I lift my face"
- **EMET:** "how would-I-lift-up my-face to Yo'av"
- **LOGOS:** "How then could I lift my face to Joab"
- **PNEUMA:** "How could I ever face your brother Joab?"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "How could I then lift my face to your brother Joab?" — combines LOGOS's formal syntax with the kinship reference.

### V.23 — "belly" vs. "belly" vs. "belly"
- All three agree on the location but differ on the spear's exit.
- **EMET:** "went-out the-spear from-behind-him"
- **LOGOS:** "the spear came out through his back"
- **PNEUMA:** "it punched out through his back"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the spear came out through his back" — LOGOS rendering is accurate without PNEUMA's added force.

### V.27 — Joab's oath
- **EMET:** "if you-had-spoken, then from the-morning would-have-gone-up the-people"
- **LOGOS:** "if you had not spoken, the people would not have given up the pursuit...until morning"
- **PNEUMA:** "if you hadn't spoken up, my men would have kept pursuing...until dawn"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "if you had not spoken, the people would not have stopped pursuing their brothers until the morning." The *lule* construction is the crux — LOGOS/PNEUMA correctly interpret it as a contrary-to-fact conditional.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
